name: percentage-square
title: Percentage square
tagline: 10×10 hundred-square shaded for a percentage with derived decimal, fraction and multiplier; models increase/decrease and forward or reverse percentage.
description: A 10×10 hundred-square (100 unit cells, each worth 1%) with a reading-order run of cells shaded to model a percentage, beside a derived readout. You write the percentage; the model shades the cells, and computes the decimal, the reduced fraction and the multiplier (35% → 0.35 = 7/20, ×0.35). Set change to "increase" or "decrease" to model a percentage change: an increase draws the whole 100% in blue plus the extra cells in amber (a 120% total, ×1.2), a decrease draws the whole with the lost cells struck out in amber (leaving 85%, ×0.85). Supply a known amount and the model finds the answer — forward (a percentage of an amount, or the amount after a change) when the value is the original, or backward (reverse percentage — find the original) when the value is the result. Fractional percentages shade a partial cell (12.5% = twelve and a half cells = 0.125 = 1/8). Cells, multiplier, decimal, fraction and answer occlude independently, so one figure asks "what percentage is shaded?", "what is the multiplier?", "write it as a fraction", or "what is the amount?".
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever a percentage is taught on the hundred-square: writing a percentage as a fraction and a decimal, the multiplier method, a percentage of an amount, percentage increase and decrease, and reverse percentage. Write `percent` (the percentage modelled, or the size of a change); the cells, multiplier, decimal and fraction are all derived. Common configurations: equivalence — percent alone shades that many cells and shows "35% = 0.35 = 7/20" with the ×0.35 multiplier (use a fractional percent like 12.5 to land a tidy fraction, 1/8); percentage of amount — add known { value, represents: "original" } to compute value × multiplier ("£80 × 0.35 = £28"); increase / decrease — set change to "increase" or "decrease"; the amber cells are the change, the multiplier becomes 1 ± percent/100, and known { represents: "original" } gives the new amount; reverse — known { represents: "result" } labels the shaded figure with the known "after" value and the model divides to find the original ("£72 ÷ 1.2 = £60"); answer space — percent 0 (an empty square) with the instruction in the header, or show.equivalence / show.multiplier false to strip the readout; question — occlude the multiplier, the fraction, the decimal, the percent, or the answer. Use known.prefix "£" / "$" for money and known.suffix for units (" kg"). Keep percent ≤ 100 for a change (a bigger increase would run off the page) and remember each cell is exactly 1%. Staged builds read very well: open on the labelled square, shade the whole, bring the amber change in, then reveal the multiplier and the answer last. Sibling boundary: for number PROPERTIES shaded on a hundred-square (multiples, primes, sequences) use number/number-grid; for a part-whole BAR or a ratio share use number/bar-model; for a fraction of a shape use number/fraction-shape. Synonyms a teacher might use: percentage, percent, per cent, hundred square, hundredths, percentage of an amount, multiplier, decimal multiplier, percentage increase, percentage decrease, percentage change, reverse percentage, original amount, fraction decimal percentage, FDP.

percent.description: The percentage the square models. With no `change` it is the proportion shaded (35 → 35 cells of 100). With a `change` it is the SIZE of the increase or decrease (20 with change "increase" → a 120% total). May be fractional — 12.5 shades twelve and a half cells. Plain percentages above 100 draw extra rows; for a change keep it ≤ 100 (a larger increase is clamped so the grid stays on the page).

change.description: Model a percentage CHANGE instead of a plain proportion. Omit for a plain percentage. "increase": the whole 100% is shaded blue and `percent` extra cells are appended in amber — the total is (100 + percent)%, multiplier 1 + percent/100. "decrease": the whole is shaded and the last `percent` cells are struck out in amber, leaving (100 − percent)% blue — multiplier 1 − percent/100. Amber always marks the change.

known.description: A single known amount to turn the figure into a numeric problem. Omit for a pure proportion / equivalence figure. The model derives the unknown amount from this value and the multiplier — there is nowhere to author the answer.

value.description: The known quantity (money or measure). What it labels is set by `represents`.

represents.description: "original" (default): the value is 100% — the original whole. The model works FORWARD to value × multiplier (a percentage of an amount, or the amount after a change). "result": the value labels the shaded figure (the part, or the amount AFTER a change). The model works BACKWARD, dividing by the multiplier to find the original — a REVERSE percentage.

prefix.description: A unit symbol written before every amount, e.g. "£" or "$". Default none.

suffix.description: A unit written after every amount, e.g. " kg" or " m". Default none.

occlude.description: Hide a readout as "?" — the question hooks. The shading itself always stays visible, so the pupil reads the square to answer. Each flag is independent; default all false.

percent.description: Hide the headline percentage ("what percentage is shaded?"). Default false.

decimal.description: Hide the decimal equivalent ("write it as a decimal"). Default false.

fraction.description: Hide the fraction equivalent ("write it as a fraction"). Default false.

multiplier.description: Hide the multiplier ("what do you multiply by?"). Default false.

answer.description: Hide the computed amount — the forward result or the reverse original ("what is the amount?"). Only meaningful with `known`. Default false.

equivalence.description: Show the "percent% = decimal = fraction" line beneath the square. Default true.

multiplier.description: Show the "Multiplier × …" line. Default true. The signature readout of this model.

guides.description: Draw the heavier every-five-cells division lines that help count the square in fives and tens. Default true.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the square; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the readout, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

examples.label: Worked example — 35% of £80 with the multiplier
Answer space — an empty hundred-square to shade 25%
Occluded question — decrease £80 by 15%, multiplier and answer hidden
Hard case — reverse percentage on an increase (after +20% it is £30 000)
Equivalence — 12.5% as a decimal and a fraction (a partial cell)
